prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: The round-1 exchange left the substance of my view unchanged: B027 is a complete discovery arc, from Holst's incretin and gut-hormone physiology and Drucker's proglucagon-derived peptide and receptor biology to Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, followed by drugs with large, independently replicated outcome benefit in glycaemia, body weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Nothing in the other five statements disputes maturity or efficacy; the whole disagreement is about credit and citation wording. Because all six round-1 configurations are the same trio, I am treating the remaining work as testing the third slot and the citation, not as seeking agreement. I have now settled on a one-part prize. A second part would need a name-set that fits under the three-person cap, and B027 already uses all three places. Splitting B027 to make room would drop a core physiologist, which would damage the strongest claim on the list to accommodate a weaker one.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point and I do not think the supplied materials resolve it. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, Habener is outside the credited names and may have a comparable claim, and Knudsen's long-acting analogue design is decisive for the drugs in clinical use. Whichever three we name, someone with a substantial claim is left out. A citation anchored in discovery risks reading as detached from the therapies that changed practice. I also acknowledge that the round-1 argument for Mojsov over Knudsen, which I share, rests on a discovery-versus-development principle that is a judgment and not a fact, and that principle is open to challenge, as Wahren-Herlenius noted.

responses.point: Sandberg moved from Knudsen in her opening trio to Mojsov in round 1, and says Mojsov's relative weight is the least certain element, and that the citation must name therapy explicitly so that omitting Knudsen is not read as dismissing drug development.
responses.response: I agree with the citation point and have adopted it: my citation ends with the clause that the discoveries made incretin-based treatment possible, so therapy is acknowledged by what the discoveries enabled, without naming the analogue designer. I do not think that fully answers your own doubt on Mojsov, and I would not claim it does. Where I stay with you is that the swap to Knudsen would put a company development contribution in place of a discovery contribution, and the chair's question on the third slot should be settled by the record on the active fragment, not by what makes the citation tidy. If that record showed Mojsov's priority to be unsupportable I would reopen the slot, and Knudsen would then be the first name I would test, but I do not have evidence that does that.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius accepts discovery versus development as framing but not as a hard rule, since the same logic would count against B036, and asks that the committee state openly that the configuration leaves out a contested contributor.
responses.response: You are right that I cannot hold the discovery-versus-development line as categorical, and I withdraw any implication that it is. My position is narrower: in B027 the discovery steps are within the credited names, so there is a discovery claim that does not depend on the analogue work, whereas the strength of B036 is mostly the translational proof of concept, with the underlying cytokine biology and the antibody engineering outside the credited pair. On your second point I fully agree. The discussion record, and ideally the citation context, should say that Habener and Knudsen are not covered by this configuration and that the allocation is a judgment, not a settled priority finding. I would keep B036 as an alternative in your sense, but I do not rank it above B039 or B014.

responses.point: Perlmann holds that the citation should be anchored in physiology, that B039's credited trio mixes Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer with the CD19 CAR work of June and Sadelain and omits Eshhar, and that B014 is a clean but basic-science alternative.
responses.response: I accept your sharper reading of B039. Rosenberg's TIL and adoptive transfer work and the June and Sadelain CAR designs are different achievements, and a citation that merged them or skipped the chimeric receptor concept would be hard to defend, which is stronger than my round-1 wording of a footnote-level credit issue. I therefore keep B039 as an alternative only, and my answer to the chair's last question is that this credit issue cannot be resolved from the supplied materials, so B039 should not enter a preferred configuration this year. On B014 I think you are right that its cleanest role would be as a second part beside a clinical achievement, but a second part means reducing B027 below three names, and I do not want to do that. I would take B014 as the fallback if B027 stalled on allocation, not as an add-on.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, notes that a single GLP-1 part leaves no room for a second achievement, so B014 would have to wait, and asks whether the committee prefers one broad GLP-1 prize or a two-part prize.
responses.response: I considered the two-part route seriously and I decline it for now. The cost is real, since B014 is the cleanest attribution on the list and it would wait. But a two-part prize needs a smaller GLP-1 configuration, and I do not see a version of B027 that remains defensible with two names: the physiology claim needs Holst and Drucker, and dropping Mojsov removes the active-peptide step, while dropping either of the others removes physiology. Waiting a year with a mature, clean candidate like B014 seems preferable to cutting the strongest claim. I also agree with your caution that credit logic for B039 should be stated explicitly if it is ever pursued.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov, Habener or Knudsen has the strongest claim for the third slot cannot be settled from the supplied list, and the committee has no documentary record in front of it on the active GLP-1 fragment.
Whether the citation should stay anchored in physiology and the active peptide, as I now propose, or explicitly credit long-acting drug development, which would be hard to do without naming Knudsen.
Whether the exclusion of the unnamed contributors, Habener and Knudsen, should be recorded in the committee's own deliberation notes so that the trio is not presented as uncontested.
Whether B039 could ever be defended with the credited trio, given the Eshhar question and the difference between Rosenberg's work and CAR design.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I disclose the spatial-transcriptomics and single-cell work in my profile, my listed co-authors (Castelo-Branco, Betsholtz, Ernfors, Frisen, Lundeberg and Kharchenko), and, relevant to this committee, eight co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg on the OpenAlex record, which I have not independently audited. None of these people is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and I have no documented tie to Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen or the credited names of B039 and B014.
